metadata.note: The Lehigh Valley Railroad main line, Jersey City to Buffalo -- 448 miles, the route of the Black Diamond Express (launched 18 May 1896, 'the Handsomest Train in the World'), which famously made no stops between Sayre, Pa. and Geneva, N.Y. The line was built outward from the anthracite country in stages: Easton-Allentown opened 11 June 1855 and Allentown-Mauch Chunk that September, the White Haven-Wilkes-Barre extension in 1866, Wilkes-Barre to Waverly, N.Y. by 1867, and the Buffalo extension in phases from 1876 to 1892, reaching Batavia on 31 August 1892. From Easton it follows the Lehigh River up through Bethlehem, Allentown, Slatington, Lehighton and Mauch Chunk (Jim Thorpe), climbs the Lehigh Gorge past Penn Haven Junction and Rockport to White Haven and over Mountain Top into Wilkes-Barre, then runs down the Susquehanna through Pittston, Tunkhannock, Towanda and Athens to Sayre and Waverly. North of Waverly the 1892 trunk runs Van Etten - Odessa - Watkins Glen and then up the EAST shore of Seneca Lake through Seneca County (Hector, Valois, Lodi, Willard, Romulus), which is how it avoided the steep grades in and out of Ithaca, before reaching Geneva, Phelps, Shortsville, Rochester Junction, Caledonia, Batavia, Alden, Lancaster, Depew and Buffalo. GEOMETRY REBUILT (2026-08-24): the Easton-Buffalo half, previously a hand-placed chain of ~17 waypoints with straight hops of up to 54 km, is now traced on real OpenStreetMap track. An earlier version of this file described the route as passing Himrod on the way north; Himrod and Dresden are in Yates County on the WEST shore of Seneca Lake, so that waypoint has been replaced with the east-shore Seneca County towns the cited source actually describes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates, not from real timetables. FOLLOW-UP FIX (2026-08-24): the 2026-08-24 rebuild above left a real bug in the Hector-Romulus stretch -- the traced path went out along a dead-end spur/siding twice and doubled straight back over itself, drawing as a visible tangled knot on the map. Fixed by re-tracing that ~5 km stretch cleanly along the same abandoned LV grade. The same follow-up pass also went through and honestly itemized six previously-unflagged straight-line gaps (central NJ, Tunkhannock-Meshoppen PA, Rochester Junction-Caledonia NY -- the largest at 13.2 mi -- LeRoy-Batavia, Batavia-Alexander, and Depew-Buffalo) in the feature's own geometry_quality field; none of these are newly introduced, they simply weren't documented before. See geometry_quality for details and mileage on each.

metadata.labelling: 2026-08-24: every feature in this file carries 'Lehigh Valley Railroad' at the start of its `line` field, which is what app.js shows in the hover tooltip, so LV routes are identifiable on the map without opening the data. Predecessor companies that were independent at the time are labelled '<Company> (Lehigh Valley predecessor)' rather than being relabelled as LV, because they were not yet Lehigh Valley in the years those features cover.
metadata.water_audit: 2026-08-24: the main line was found crossing Seneca Lake at two places (up to 1.3 km from shore) because the east-shore stretch was drawn as long straight chords. Re-traced; verified zero water crossings against OpenStreetMap lake multipolygons. Note the lake polygons must be assembled from their relation members -- Seneca Lake's outer ring is split across 17 ways and Cayuga's across 13, and treating each member as its own closed ring gives badly wrong results.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.elmira_cortland_split: 2026-10-18, per research/branches/elmira_cortland_and_northern_railroad.txt: the single feature lv-elmira-cortland-branch (Elmira - Canastota, segments 1878-1884, 1884-1896, 1896-1911, 1911-1932, 1932-1948, 1948-1954; a 186-point line with no geometry_quality) drew 18 pre-1896 years in Lehigh Valley colour although the LV did not run the trains until Feb 20 1896, and drew Elmira - East Ithaca to 1954 although its passenger service ended in 1935. Replaced by four LV features on re-traced OSM geometry, each drawn once per year: Elmira - East Ithaca 1896-1935 (was to 1954, 19 years overstated), East Ithaca - Cortland 1896-1950 (was to 1954), Cortland - Canastota 1896-1950 [OPEN] (keeps the id lv-elmira-cortland-branch; was to 1954 - MAR's 1954 conflicts with the Sept 1951 Guide), and the previously missing Canastota - Camden 1896-1935. The 1878-1896 years moved to elmira_cortland_and_northern_railroad.geojson in the EC&N's and its predecessors' own colours (EC&N 1884-1896; UI&E 1872-1884; CC&D 1878-1884; C&C 1870-1878). Notes corrected: the EC&N was formed Mar 7 1884, not 1878; the LV operated the line from 1896, not 'somewhat separately until 1905'; Apr 25 1948 dropped only the DeRuyter milk trains, not all passenger service; the post-1948 trains were steam/diesel mixed trains with a combine, not a gas-electric; Van Etten - Spencer own track was abandoned c.1933 (MAR, Wikipedia), not 1932.

properties.line: Lehigh Valley: Main Line (Jersey City – Buffalo)
properties.speed_source: estimated: blended across the line's history, from modest 1870s-80s running times to the Black Diamond's ~8.5-hour Jersey City-Buffalo schedule by the early-mid 20th century; unsourced

segments.note: The LV's original Easton-Allentown-Bethlehem segment opened in 1855 (Allentown's first rail service, extended to Mauch Chunk/Jim Thorpe that September); the railroad grew northwest toward Wilkes-Barre and beyond over the following decades under Asa Packer. Through Jersey City-Buffalo service became available via connecting lines by 1876, with LV completing its own wholly-owned line all the way to Buffalo in 1892. Frequency in this early era estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: The flagship Black Diamond Express launched May 18, 1896 (Jersey City-Buffalo, with a Hudson ferry connection onward to Manhattan), nicknamed 'the Handsomest Train in the World' and 'the Honeymoon Express', competing with the Lackawanna and New York Central for Buffalo-bound traffic. Aggregate corridor frequency (Black Diamond plus other named and local trains) estimated at this era's peak. Jersey City terminal used PRR's Exchange Place until 1913, then CNJ's Communipaw Terminal (the endpoint plotted here); from 1918 through-trains were rerouted to Penn Station in Manhattan, with some locals still using Communipaw.

segments.note: The Black Diamond was re-equipped with the line's first streamlined lightweight coaches in 1938. Postwar decline set in as competition from faster Lackawanna and NYC service, plus cars and planes, eroded ridership; the Black Diamond was discontinued in 1959, and the perennially marginal Lehigh Valley Railroad exited the passenger business entirely by the early 1960s. Buffalo trains used a new LV terminal at Scott & Main (Canalside area, the endpoint plotted here) from 1916 until it was demolished in 1955 for the Niagara Thruway, after which LV moved to a smaller outlying station until 1961.

properties.geometry_quality: Watkins Glen - Geneva RE-TRACED 2026-08-24 (east shore of Seneca Lake -- see below for a further fix to this same stretch, same date). This stretch up the east shore of Seneca Lake was previously a handful of coarse waypoints with chords of 5.2, 8.3 and 9.4 miles, two of which cut across Seneca Lake by up to 1.3 km. It is now real OpenStreetMap track from Hector north through Valois, Willard and Romulus to Geneva, plus two legs -- Odessa-Watkins Glen and Watkins Glen-Hector (~5.3 mi and ~2.8 mi) -- where no connected OSM alignment survives and the line is instead drawn following the lake's east shore at a 500 m margin, which keeps it on land and on the correct side. BACKTRACK FIXED 2026-08-24: the Hector-Romulus stretch just re-traced above (Seneca County, roughly 42.62-42.71N) contained a real bug -- the traced path ran out along a dead-end spur or siding twice and doubled directly back over itself both times (an out-and-back retrace, not a loop), which drew as a visible tangled knot on the map. Replaced with a clean 5.04 km path along the same abandoned LV grade (OSM old_railway_operator=LV), verified free of self-intersections; ratio to straight-line is 1.05. REMAINING UNFLAGGED STRAIGHT-LINE GAPS, found and documented 2026-08-24 (none of these existed as connected OSM track at time of writing; each is a straight chord between confirmed real-track endpoints, not a traced alignment): central New Jersey, Newark area through Roselle and North Edison to Bound Brook, three consecutive hops totaling ~21.2 mi; Tunkhannock to Meshoppen, PA, ~7.3 mi; Rochester Junction (Town of Mendon) to Caledonia, NY, ~13.2 mi -- the largest single gap on the route, investigated 2026-08-24: real abandoned-LV-tagged fragments exist on both sides but do not connect through OSM's data even via the nearby Rochester Branch, so no real-track alternative to the straight line was found; LeRoy to Batavia, NY, ~5.7 mi; Batavia to Brookville (Town of Alexander), NY, ~5.3 mi; Depew to South Buffalo, NY, ~6.5 mi. Total traced length is 455.7 mi against the 448 mi documented for the full route, a reasonable match given these gaps. No leg draws a later-era alignment than its own era. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 1 ruled segment totalling 13 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).

geometry_repairs.method: Overpass rail graph, 8.0 km corridor, Dijkstra, simplified to 3.0 m; 1.18 mi bridged across gaps in OSM

properties.line: Lehigh Valley: Elmira and Cortland Branch (Elmira – East Ithaca)
properties.speed_source: estimated for a rural branch of local passenger, milk and mixed trains (steam, later diesel road-switchers with a combine on the mixed trains); no running times were read. Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-18), routed with opstrace.py on ways tagged old_railway_operator=LV named 'Elmira and Cortland Branch' (abandoned/razed/dismantled grade) and the rail-trails on that grade (Dryden Rail Trail, East Ithaca Recreation Way, East Hill Recreation Way, Cazenovia South Trail, Link Trail, Gorge Trail), plus untagged OpenHistoricalMap railway ways east of Brooktondale. Simplified with douglas_peucker(8 m) + trim_reversals.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 49.3 mi against 50.2 mi documented (MAR MP 0.5-50.7). Built from: Elmira - Horseheads 4.4 mi on the OSM 'Elmira and Cortland branch' grade, i.e. the Canal Railroad alignment of 1881 (MAR 0.5-5.6 = 5.1 mi; the drawn line starts at the south end of the mapped grade at about Elmira's Fifth St, which is MAR's MP 0.5 station area, and Horseheads is pinned on the grade at the village, so the 0.7 mi shortfall is the waypoint, not the route); Horseheads - Van Etten 19.5 mi on the E&C grade via Breesport, Erin, Park Station and Swartwood (MAR 5.6-25.2 = 19.6 mi; AR 24.7 mi Elmira - Van Etten); Van Etten - Spencer - East Ithaca 25.3 mi (MAR 25.2-50.7 = 25.5 mi): the branch's OWN Van Etten - Spencer track (built early 1876), then the E&C grade via West Candor, Willseyville, Brooktondale and Besemer to the East Ithaca (Maple Ave) station site; about 1.1 mi near Besemer-East Ithaca is on untagged OpenHistoricalMap railway ways that follow the same grade. No straight-line legs. LATER/OTHER-ALIGNMENT NOTE: from c.1933 to 1935 Van Etten - Spencer trains ran on the Ithaca Branch main track, but the whole span is drawn on the branch's own (abandoned c.1933) track about 0.2-0.6 km away.

segments.note: Lehigh Valley bought the Elmira, Cortland & Northern on Feb 20 1896 and operated it from that day: the EC&N's top officials were dismissed, its engines renumbered into the LV 900 series, the line became the LV's Elmira and Cortland Branch in the Auburn Division, and the 1899 public timetable is an LV one (MAR ch.6). The EC&N survived only as a paper company until the formal merger of 1905, which changed nothing about who ran the trains. On Jan 1 1900 two passenger and two mixed/freight trains ran each way Elmira - Canastota, and from May 27 1900 both Elmira trains ran through to Camden (MAR ch.10). From 1903 the Canastota - Sayre milk trains carried passengers on Sundays only. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable reading.
sources: Segment-level: start from MAR ch.6 (LV operation from Feb 20 1896); 1900 service from MAR ch.10; 1931 boundary from MAR ch.12 (April 1931 morning trains withdrawn) (dates as extracted from MAR by research/branches/elmira_cortland_and_northern_railroad.txt; the tracer did not re-read MAR). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: From April 1931 the morning through trains were withdrawn; by 1933 the afternoon trains were replaced by daily-except-Sunday MIXED trains 825/826 Elmira - Van Etten (passengers carried), and from 1933 the passenger-carrying milk trains 324/325 (Canastota - Sayre) ran Van Etten - Spencer - East Ithaca. In c.1933 the branch's own Van Etten - Spencer track was abandoned and trains used the parallel Ithaca Branch main track (MAR and Wikipedia give 1933; an earlier note here said 1932). Scheduled trains between Elmira and Van Etten were discontinued in the spring of 1935, and on June 30 1935 Train 325 made its last trip north over Spencer - East Ithaca (MAR ch.12). Freight only afterwards and NOT drawn: Horseheads - Van Etten to June 25 1938, Elmira - Horseheads to 1975 (MAR ch.12, Abandoned Rails). The dead line carried detoured trains briefly in the July 1935 flood - not regular service. headway_min is an ESTIMATE, not a timetable reading.
